# Peak Visualization {.divider}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · Day 01]{.eyebrow}


<!-- slide · peaks theory -->
## What Is a Peak {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · theory]{.eyebrow}

### Signal piled up at a genomic position

A peak is a region where sequencing reads pile up: a transcription factor bound there (ChIP-seq), the chromatin was open (ATAC-seq), or a histone carried a mark. The standard view is a **genome browser**: each assay a horizontal signal track, stacked over a shared coordinate, with genes annotated underneath.

The reading skill is combinatorial. **H3K4me3** marks active promoters, **H3K27ac** marks active promoters *and* enhancers, **ATAC** marks any open chromatin. So a region that is open and acetylated but lacks H3K4me3 is an **enhancer**, not a promoter. We'll build that exact comparison.


<!-- slide · peaks data -->
## Peaks · The Data {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks]{.eyebrow}

### Three signal tracks + a gene table

`load_peaks()` is the signal, one row per genomic position, one column per mark. `load_peak_genes()` is the annotation track: where each gene sits and which strand it's on.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
from genomics_course.data import load_peaks, load_peak_genes

sig = load_peaks()              # position, H3K27ac, H3K4me3, ATAC
genes = load_peak_genes()       # name, start, end, strand
sig.head(3)
```


<!-- slide · peaks step 1 -->
## Peaks · Step 1 — One Track {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · Fill the area under one signal

A signal track is just `fill_between(position, signal)`. Drop the frame so the genomic axis reads cleanly. Three clear H3K27ac peaks appear, two promoters and one enhancer.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "6-7"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 3.0
from genomics_course.data import load_peaks

sig = load_peaks()                                       # position, H3K27ac, H3K4me3, ATAC

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 3.0))
ax.fill_between(sig.position, sig.H3K27ac, color=GREEN, alpha=.85, lw=0)  # area under the signal
ax.set_ylabel("H3K27ac"); ax.set_xlabel("genomic position (bp)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide · peaks step 2 -->
## Peaks · Step 2 — Stack the Marks {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · One subplot per mark, shared x-axis

Stack the three marks as rows with `sharex=True` so positions line up. Now you compare marks vertically: the middle peak is missing from the H3K4me3 row.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "6-8,11-13"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.2
from genomics_course.data import load_peaks

sig = load_peaks()
marks = ["H3K27ac", "H3K4me3", "ATAC"]                   # plotting order, top to bottom
mark_pal = {"H3K27ac": GREEN, "H3K4me3": PURPLE, "ATAC": AMBER}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(marks), 1, figsize=(6.6, 4.2),  # one row per mark
                         sharex=True,                    # align genomic coordinates
                         gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.15})
for ax, m in zip(axes, marks):                           # draw each mark in its row
    ax.fill_between(sig.position, sig[m], color=mark_pal[m], alpha=.85, lw=0)
    ax.set_ylabel(m, fontsize=8); ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    for s in ["top", "right", "bottom"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
axes[-1].set_xlabel("genomic position (bp)")
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide · peaks step 3 -->
## Peaks · Step 3 — The Gene Track {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · build]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · Annotate genes underneath with strand

Add a short track at the bottom and draw each gene as an arrow pointing in its strand direction (`FancyArrow`). Now the peaks have context: which sit over a gene's start (its TSS).

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "2,9,16-23"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.6
from genomics_course.data import load_peaks, load_peak_genes
from matplotlib.patches import FancyArrow                # arrow = gene body + strand

sig = load_peaks(); genes = load_peak_genes()
marks = ["H3K27ac", "H3K4me3", "ATAC"]
mark_pal = {"H3K27ac": GREEN, "H3K4me3": PURPLE, "ATAC": AMBER}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(marks) + 1, 1, figsize=(6.6, 4.6), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [3, 3, 3, 1.1], "hspace": 0.15})
for ax, m in zip(axes, marks):
    ax.fill_between(sig.position, sig[m], color=mark_pal[m], alpha=.85, lw=0)
    ax.set_ylabel(m, fontsize=8); ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    for s in ["top", "right", "bottom"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
gax = axes[-1]                                           # the gene annotation row
for _, g in genes.iterrows():
    x0 = g.start if g.strand == "+" else g.end           # arrow tail at the 5' end
    dx = (g.end - g.start) * (1 if g.strand == "+" else -1)  # points along the strand
    gax.add_patch(FancyArrow(x0, 0.5, dx, 0, width=0.18, length_includes_head=True,
                             head_width=0.4, head_length=500, color=MUTED, zorder=3))
    gax.text((g.start + g.end) / 2, 0.95, g["name"], ha="center", fontsize=7,
             fontweight="bold", color=INK)
gax.set_ylim(0, 1.4); gax.set_yticks([]); gax.set_ylabel("genes", fontsize=8)
gax.set_xlabel("genomic position (bp)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: gax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide · peaks step 4 -->
## Peaks · Step 4 — Highlight the Enhancer {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · build]{.eyebrow}

### 4 · Shade the region, name the finding

Draw an `axvspan` across every track at the middle peak and title with the call. The shaded column is high in H3K27ac and ATAC but flat in H3K4me3: an active **enhancer**, not a promoter.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "12,18,25-26"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.6
from genomics_course.data import load_peaks, load_peak_genes
from matplotlib.patches import FancyArrow

sig = load_peaks(); genes = load_peak_genes()
marks = ["H3K27ac", "H3K4me3", "ATAC"]
mark_pal = {"H3K27ac": GREEN, "H3K4me3": PURPLE, "ATAC": AMBER}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(marks) + 1, 1, figsize=(6.6, 4.6), sharex=True,
                         gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [3, 3, 3, 1.1], "hspace": 0.15})
for ax, m in zip(axes, marks):
    ax.fill_between(sig.position, sig[m], color=mark_pal[m], alpha=.85, lw=0)
    ax.axvspan(8100, 8900, color=AMBER, alpha=.12, zorder=0)   # highlight the enhancer
    ax.set_ylabel(m, fontsize=8); ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    for s in ["top", "right", "bottom"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
gax = axes[-1]
gax.axvspan(8100, 8900, color=AMBER, alpha=.12, zorder=0)      # same column on the gene track
for _, g in genes.iterrows():
    x0 = g.start if g.strand == "+" else g.end
    dx = (g.end - g.start) * (1 if g.strand == "+" else -1)
    gax.add_patch(FancyArrow(x0, 0.5, dx, 0, width=0.18, length_includes_head=True,
                             head_width=0.4, head_length=500, color=MUTED, zorder=3))
    gax.text((g.start + g.end) / 2, 0.95, g["name"], ha="center", fontsize=7,
             fontweight="bold", color=INK)
gax.set_ylim(0, 1.4); gax.set_yticks([]); gax.set_ylabel("genes", fontsize=8)
gax.set_xlabel("genomic position (bp)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: gax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
fig.suptitle("ENHANCER: OPEN + ACETYLATED, NO H3K4me3",       # title = the finding
             fontweight="bold", color="#333333")
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
[The bottom line]{.tl}
A browser view is **one fill_between per mark → stack with shared x → annotate genes → highlight the region**. The marks read combinatorially: H3K27ac + ATAC + H3K4me3 = active promoter; H3K27ac + ATAC but **no** H3K4me3 = enhancer.
:::


<!-- slide · peaks pygenometracks -->
## The Production Tool · pyGenomeTracks {.smaller}

[ChIP / ATAC peaks · reference]{.eyebrow}

### Real bigWig/BED, driven by a config

From scratch is great for teaching; for real data you'd use **pyGenomeTracks**, a CLI that renders a browser figure from an INI config pointing at your `.bw`/`.bed`/`.gtf` files. Same mental model, production inputs.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# pip install pyGenomeTracks   (reads real bigWig / BED / GTF, not in-memory arrays)
config = """
[H3K27ac]
file = H3K27ac.bw
color = #379A8B
height = 3
[H3K4me3]
file = H3K4me3.bw
color = #9A607F
height = 3
[genes]
file = genes.gtf
height = 1.5
"""
open("tracks.ini", "w").write(config)

# render a region to a figure from the shell:
#   pyGenomeTracks --tracks tracks.ini --region chr1:1000000-1020000 -o region.pdf
```
